label: Stepped etching
style: Style direction: stepped miniature woodcut. Distinctive angular canopies and roof patterns, asymmetric foliage clusters, clipped diagonal corners, two or three deliberate internal lines per object, expressive but very sparse marks. White forms with strong black lower edges and very limited gray.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: pixel sprite source atlas for a real 1-bit handheld top-down RPG, not a scene illustration.
Create ONE source sheet on genuinely transparent background, exactly FOUR columns by FOUR rows, 16 separated sprites total. Each equal source cell represents a 64x64 native-pixel workspace with generous transparent gutters. The objects themselves have the native sizes listed below; ground squares are small 16x16 sprites in their cells, not enlarged to fill the frame. Pixel art drawn as large crisp square pixel blocks, no smooth rendering. Only opaque black, opaque white and a single medium gray (#999999) inside sprites. Preserve opaque white interiors. Gray only for selective small shadow masses; do not fill ground with gray. No antialiasing, no gradients, no tiny illustrative detail, no existing art references.
EXACT row-major asset list:
Row 1: (1) grass ground, an opaque borderless 16x16 white square with two sparse dark grass tufts; (2) packed dirt ground, opaque borderless 16x16 white square with a few dark flecks; (3) cave floor, opaque borderless 16x16 black square with three tiny white chips; (4) paving ground, opaque borderless 16x16 white square with sparse stepped masonry joints.
Row 2: (5) water, opaque borderless 16x16 black square with two simple white wave strokes; (6) cave rock wall, opaque 16x16 tile with a few large stone faces, black seams and selective gray; (7) small flower patch, transparent 16x16 prop; (8) vegetable bed, transparent 16x16 prop.
Row 3: (9) one complete broadleaf tree, 32x32 pixels, clear rounded crown, trunk visible; (10) one complete pine, 16x32 pixels; (11) bush, 16x16 pixels; (12) boulder, 16x16 pixels.
Row 4: (13) cottage, 48x32 pixels, top-down RPG front view with roof above a wall, centered visible door, one window, no ground shadow outside footprint; (14) taller city shop, 48x48 pixels, flat stepped roof, simple windows, stripe awning and centered entrance, top-down RPG front view; (15) streetlamp, 16x32 pixels; (16) crystal, 16x16 pixels.
The entire source atlas is a production sprite kit, not 16 miniature scenes. Every object stays isolated inside its own cell. Transparent gaps between all cells; NO gridlines, no borders, no checkerboard drawn into the image, no labels, no player, no text, no watermark. Repeated ground tiles should not have visible box outlines. The cottage, shop and tree will be sliced into 16x16 tiles for reuse throughout a connected world. Strong readable silhouettes at actual native size are more important than detail.
Style direction: stepped miniature woodcut. Distinctive angular canopies and roof patterns, asymmetric foliage clusters, clipped diagonal corners, two or three deliberate internal lines per object, expressive but very sparse marks. White forms with strong black lower edges and very limited gray.
